Name: recall_success_dissociation
Title: Recall Ranks Retrievers, Success Does Not: A Two-Environment Audit of Experience Retrieval Against the Static Prompt with Manipulated Duplicate Availability
Short Hypothesis: Retriever recall (fraction of top-k items sharing the test task's type or binding) and the task-success residual over the best static prompt built from the same bank dissociate, and the dissociation is set by whether the retrieved binding is recoverable inside the episode. On ALFWorld the measured +17.2 net of BM25 k=3 over static3 is an exemplar-source effect, not a recall effect: a static prompt of three fixed self-generated bank exemplars of the goal's type sits within the ±8 floor of BM25, and above type recall the map is flat through same-scene recall (oracle same-scene at coverage 0/0.5/1) and exact same-game duplicates, because layout and object location are recoverable by looking. On WebShop, where the binding (which product satisfies the attribute set) is expensive to recover by search, the residual over the best static arm appears only when a same-product trajectory is in the bank, rises with the fraction of instructions for which one is retrieved (coverage 0/0.5/1), and the natural BM25 retriever's gain equals its measured product recall times the oracle gain. Recall above the type threshold is therefore uninformative unless the bank carries non-recoverable bindings, and retriever evaluation must report the success residual over a static arm built from the same bank at two or more duplicate-availability levels.
Related Work: 2604.04949 trains retrievers from agent trajectories and reports evidence recall and task success together with no random or fixed control, so recall and success are never dissociated. 2512.20854 correlates retrieval metrics with LLM-judged answer quality in RAG QA and 2508.05909 tries to isolate the retriever's contribution to a reader; both are single-turn QA with no static arm. 2603.02473 finds retrieval dominates write strategy on LoCoMo (QA, no full-history or fixed arm). SWE-ContextBench (2602.08316) shows correctly selected related-task experience helps and mis-selected experience harms on dependency-linked tasks, without a random or static control; 2607.10608 shows wrong retrieved memory is adopted at the first decision point. Traj-Bootstrap (2505.00234) and ExpeL/Reflexion report ALFWorld and WebShop memory gains over no memory only. Measurement A on this node observed unseen approximately equal to seen with one retriever and no static arm. Measurement C on this node (274 x 2) measured k3 minus static3 = +17.2 net over three fixed type-conditioned expert exemplars, with no static arm built from the bank itself and no manipulation of what the retrieved items share with the test game. Archived decorative_retriever (5.75) observed retrieval-set overlap without manipulating it.
Abstract: Retrievers for agent memory are ranked by recall of relevant items; whether that ranking survives when the outcome is task success over the best static prompt built from the same experience is unknown, and it should depend on whether the retrieved item carries something the agent cannot recover inside the episode. On ALFWorld, BM25 retrieval at k=3 beats three fixed type-conditioned expert exemplars by a measured +17.2 net; we claim this residual is an exemplar-source effect, not a recall effect. We manipulate two things on two environments with Qwen3-32B: retriever recall (random-type, same-type-random, goal-BM25, oracle same-binding, exact duplicate, all at k=3) and the bank's duplicate availability (oracle same-binding items retained for a nested 0/50/100% of test tasks: scene on ALFWorld, goal product on WebShop). Every arm is paired on (task, seed) with static arms built from the same bank (fixed bank exemplars per type and type-agnostic, compiled procedure, whole bank in a 16k context), and the comparator is selected on separate seeds or a held-out set so no residual is computed on the cells that chose its baseline. Predictions: on ALFWorld a static prompt of three fixed bank exemplars of the goal's type sits within the ±8 floor of BM25, and the residual is flat from type recall through same-scene coverage (slope within ±8 per unit coverage) and exact same-game duplicates; on WebShop, on the subset of test instructions with a same-product success in the bank, the residual rises with coverage (slope at least +16 per unit) and the natural BM25 gain equals its measured product recall times the oracle gain, while with duplicates removed no retriever clears the floor over the static arm. A positive control (BM25 over k=0 on WebShop) gates the residual-over-static claims; the coverage contrasts are comparator-free. The audit yields a rule for evaluating experience retrievers: report success residual over a static arm built from the same bank at two duplicate-availability levels, and treat recall above the type threshold as uninformative unless the bank carries bindings the episode cannot recover.
Experiments: E0 ALFWorld bank and pools (about 2,400 episodes, about 2 h): A's bank and C's arm definitions are reused; the bank is supplemented by k=0 runs (2 seeds) on train games in the valid_seen scenes so that every valid_seen game has at least one (typically three) same-type same-scene success (games without one are reported and excluded from the coverage arms; expected under 5%); the exact-duplicate pool is each valid_seen game's own k=0 or static3 success from C's seeds, defining the subset G (expected at least 80 games; one extra non-evaluation static3 seed, 140 episodes, is run if smaller). All new ALFWorld runs are on valid_seen (140 games) with fresh seeds disjoint from C's: two selection seeds (3-4) and four evaluation seeds (5-8). E1 ALFWorld static arms, 140 x 6 = 840 cells each: k0; static3 (C's three fixed type-conditioned expert exemplars, about 430 tokens); static3-bank (three fixed bank successes per type, chosen once as BM25 medoids of the type, token-matched to static3); instr_all (type-agnostic six-procedure prompt); whole-bank (bank in context up to 16k, same-type items first, shortest-first within type, rule pre-registered). Comparator rule: the static arm with the highest mean success on seeds 3-4 (280 cells; ties within 4 net resolved toward static3); all residuals are computed on seeds 5-8 only (560 cells). 4,200 episodes. E2 ALFWorld retrieval ladder at k=3, seeds 5-8, 560 cells each: random-type (uniform over the bank; type recall about 1/6); same-type-random (uniform over same-type items; type recall 1, object-class and scene recall at base rate); BM25 on goal text over the natural bank (scene recall b_alf measured); oracle-scene at coverage c in {0, 0.5, 1}: for a pre-registered nested fraction c of games the same-type same-scene items are ranked first (by BM25 score among themselves), remaining slots filled by BM25 over other scenes; c=0 is BM25 with every same-scene item excluded, so per-cell scene recall equals c by construction; oracle-game on G: the game's own success at rank 1 plus two BM25 items. 7 x 560 = 3,920 episodes. ALFWorld total about 10,500 episodes, about 10 h on one vLLM replica at about 1,100 episodes/h. E3 WebShop setup and bank (one day of setup; about 4,800 episodes, about 3.7 h): Qwen3-32B ReAct agent on the WebShop text environment; T = the 500 standard test instructions; L = train instructions whose goal product equals a test goal product (count reported), run at k=0 with two seeds, plus random train instructions at one seed up to 3,000 instructions; successes (score = 1) form the bank; S = test instructions with at least one same-product bank success, pre-registered minimum 150 and cap 250 (fallback 1: the public human demonstrations are added to the bank; fallback 2: the exact-instruction rung X becomes the primary WebShop duplicate level and is labelled as a weaker binding); a held-out set of 300 train instructions not in the bank is reserved for comparator selection; the floor replicate (k0 on T with two non-evaluation seeds, 1,000 episodes) also supplies the exact-instruction pool and the subset X of test instructions with at least one own success. E4 WebShop static arms (selection set 300 x 1 seed; T x 2 seeds; S x 2 further seeds so S has 4): k0; fixed3 (three fixed bank successes of random categories, type-agnostic, token-matched to k=3); fixed3-cat (three fixed bank successes of the instruction's product category); procedure (about 80-token compiled procedure written by rule from the bank); whole-bank (shortest-first truncation at 16k, rule pre-registered). Comparator = best mean success on the selection set; if the winner is bank-dependent (whole-bank), residuals at c<1 are also reported over the best bank-invariant family. About 8,000-9,000 episodes. E5 WebShop retrieval ladder at k=3: random, same-category-random, BM25 on instruction text over the natural bank (product recall on S, b_ws, measured), and c=0 (BM25 with same-product items removed) on T x 2 seeds and S x 2 further seeds; oracle same-product at c in {0.5, 1} over a nested pre-registered split of S (same-product item at rank 1, remaining slots BM25) on S x 4 seeds; oracle-exact on X x 4 seeds (the instruction's own k0 success at rank 1 plus two BM25 items). About 7,200-9,000 episodes. WebShop total about 20,000-23,000 episodes, 15-18 h on one replica at about 1,300 episodes/h. E6 gate: BM25 k=3 (natural bank) minus k0 on T must clear the WebShop floor before any residual-over-static claim on WebShop; the comparator-free coverage contrasts are tested regardless. E7 analysis: per arm, type or category recall and binding recall (fraction of cells with at least one same-scene or same-product item in the top-3); residual over the comparator on evaluation cells; comparator-free paired contrasts between retrieval arms; for each environment a linear slope of the paired residual (versus that family's c=0 arm) on coverage over c in {0, 0.5, 1} plus the natural BM25 point at its measured recall, with bootstrap CI (1,000 resamples over tasks, jointly across arms); prefill tokens per episode logged as cached (static prefix) and uncached (retrieved prefix), residual per uncached prefill token as the cost axis. Whole study about 32,000 episodes, about 27 replica-hours, about 14 h wall-clock on the two A100s (one vLLM replica of Qwen3-32B per GPU; ALFWorld on one replica while WebShop bank generation runs on the other, then both replicas on WebShop arms), plus the WebShop setup day.
Baselines and Ablations: Static arms first (the baseline, selected out-of-sample): ALFWorld k0, static3 (expert, type-conditioned), static3-bank (bank exemplars, type-conditioned), instr_all (type-agnostic), whole-bank; WebShop k0, fixed3 (type-agnostic), fixed3-cat (category-conditioned), procedure (type-agnostic), whole-bank (truncated). Manipulations: retriever ladder at matched k=3 (random-type or random, same-type-random or same-category-random, BM25, oracle same-binding, exact duplicate) and bank duplicate availability as oracle coverage c in {0, 0.5, 1} on both environments, with the natural bank as a fourth measured recall point. Ablations that isolate the mechanism: static3 versus static3-bank (exemplar source at fixed type recall; the manipulation claimed to remove the +17.2); same-type-random versus BM25 (object-class match versus type alone); c=0 BM25 versus natural BM25 (whether the natural retriever's same-scene or same-product hits carry anything); oracle-exact versus oracle same-binding (exact duplicate versus binding). The k=1 length ablations of the previous version are dropped: every retrieval arm has k=3 and the static exemplar arms are token-matched.
Falsifiable Predictions: P1 (ALFWorld: the +17.2 is source, not recall; 560 evaluation cells, ±8 floor). P1a: random-type k=3 sits at or below -8 net against the comparator; falsified by random-type within ±8 of the comparator, produced by the random-type arm. P1b: BM25 minus static3 replicates C on fresh seeds (at least +8; C's seen value +14.3); falsified by +8 or less, produced by the BM25 and static3 arms. P1c: static3-bank is within ±8 of BM25 k=3, i.e. the manipulation that removes the +17.2 is replacing expert exemplars with fixed bank exemplars of the same type; falsified by BM25 at least +8 over static3-bank, produced by the BM25 arm paired with static3-bank (a three-exemplar prompt cannot contain the retrieved items, so this is not entailed by inclusion). P1d: same-type-random is within ±8 of BM25; falsified by same-type-random at least 8 below BM25 (object-class match matters), produced by the same-type-random arm. P2 (ALFWorld binding flat; comparator-free paired differences): oracle-scene c=1 minus c=0 is within ±8, and oracle-game minus oracle-scene c=1 is within ±8 on G; falsified by either difference at or above +8, produced by the c=1 arm (scene recall 1 by construction, at least one same-scene same-type item in every cell) or by the oracle-game arm (exact duplicate at rank 1). The oracle-game clause is the riskiest in the proposal and is kept as the strongest test of recoverability. P3 (WebShop binding, on S with at least 600 paired cells; floor the larger of the S estimate and ±8). P3a: oracle c=1 minus c=0 on S is at least +16 net; falsified by less than +8, produced by the c=1 arm on S (a same-product trajectory at rank 1 fails to transfer the binding). P3b: BM25 (natural bank) minus BM25 c=0 on S equals b_ws times the P3a effect within ±8 (the natural retriever's gain tracks its measured product recall), claimed when b_ws is at least 0.3 (pre-registered; expected, since the same-product instruction shares attribute words); falsified by a BM25 effect at least 8 above or below that product, produced by the BM25 arm on S (above: same-product hits are not what carries the BM25 gain; below: retrieved duplicates are not used). P3c: with same-product items removed (c=0), every retriever's residual over the comparator on T is within ±8; falsified by any c=0 retriever at or above +8, produced by the c=0 BM25 or same-category-random arm (category search strategies transfer without duplicates). P3d (secondary): oracle-exact minus c=0 on X is at least +16; falsified by less than +8, produced by the oracle-exact arm. P4 (headline, cross-environment slope): the linear slope of the paired residual on coverage, fit over c in {0, 0.5, 1} plus the natural BM25 point, with the stated MDE of 16 net per unit coverage, is within ±8 on ALFWorld with a 95% bootstrap CI excluding +16, and at least +16 on WebShop (S) with a CI excluding +8. Each clause is falsified separately: ALFWorld slope at or above +16 with CI excluding +8 (scene binding is informative), produced by the c=0.5 and c=1 oracle-scene arms; WebShop slope below +8 (product binding is uninformative), produced by the c=0.5 and c=1 arms on S; two slopes both at or above +16 or both within ±8 falsify the dissociation itself. P5 (gate, positive control): BM25 k=3 over the natural bank beats k0 on T by at least the WebShop floor; if it fails, produced by E6, P3c and every WebShop residual-over-static claim are withdrawn, while P3a, P3b, P3d and the WebShop slope (all comparator-free) are still tested and reported.
Measurement and Noise Control: ALFWorld: 140 valid_seen games x 4 fresh evaluation seeds = 560 paired cells per arm, ±8 net floor (C's CI half-width for k3 minus static3 was about ±5 at 548 cells; ±8 is kept as the pre-registered floor, 0.47 of the measured +17.2 and about 0.27 of the Gate-0 gain); the comparator is selected on two separate seeds (280 cells) by a pre-registered rule, so no residual is computed on the cells that selected its baseline; manipulation effects are paired differences between retrieval arms and do not use the comparator; bootstrap CIs over games (1,000 resamples, jointly across arms). WebShop: T = 500 x 2 seeds = 1,000 cells; S at least 150 (capped at 250) x 4 seeds = 600-1,000 cells; the floor is estimated from two independent k0 replicates with different seed pairs before any claim (expected about ±6 net at 1,000 cells, about ±8 at 600) and the larger of the estimate and ±8 is used; success (score = 1) primary, WebShop score secondary; comparator selected on 300 held-out train instructions; bootstrap CIs over instructions. Slope: three coverage levels plus the natural point, per-level paired SE about 4 net, slope SE about 5.7 net per unit coverage, MDE about 16 (two-sided 0.05, 80% power); P4's thresholds are set at that MDE. Recall computed per episode from retrieved item ids and item metadata (type, scene, game; category, product id). Per-type ALFWorld and per-category WebShop results exploratory. Pre-registration before E1 of retriever definitions, the nested coverage splits, bank filters, truncation rules, the comparator rule and tie rule, the |S| minimum and the b_ws threshold, and floors.

Risk Factors and Limitations: WebShop install plus bank generation is a day and about five GPU-hours; if L is small or Qwen3-32B's WebShop success is low, S may fall below 150 even with the human demonstrations, in which case the exact-instruction rung (X) becomes the primary WebShop duplicate level and is labelled a weaker binding. The exact-duplicate rungs (oracle-game, oracle-exact) are the strongest bindings and the ALFWorld one is the riskiest clause: if oracle-game clears the floor while same-scene is flat, the criterion becomes recovery cost rather than recoverability, stated here in advance as the alternative reading, not offered afterwards as a rescue. If P1c fails (BM25 beats static3-bank by 8 or more), the ALFWorld step sits above type recall and the ladder locates it (same-type-random, c=0), but the claim that ALFWorld retrieval has no residual over a bank-built static arm is falsified; if P1d also fails, the c=1 contrast is re-run with same-scene items restricted to the goal's object class where available (exploratory) because same-scene items may displace object-matched ones. Comparator selection on 280 ALFWorld cells or 300 WebShop instructions is a point-estimate choice; a wrong choice biases residuals upward, which works against P1c and P3c, not for them. The WebShop whole-bank arm is truncated and may or may not contain the same-product item; it is reported with its truncation rule and bank-dependent comparators are handled as stated in E4. The oracle same-scene manipulation exists only on valid_seen; valid_unseen is not used in the ladder. Coverage levels 0/0.5/1 are mixtures over tasks, so the intermediate point tests per-task additivity and adds slope power rather than a new prompt type. Two environments are two points; the rule is a prediction to test on a third.
Addresses gap: G23 (memory benchmarks score recall, not downstream task success) with G22 (random or fixed selection control at matched length, here the static arm built from the same bank); cross-environment generality per the axis definition, with duplicate availability manipulated at three levels on both environments.
Not a restatement of: Brief bullet 'Retrieval on this node (Measurement A): unseen approximately equal to seen, so the retrieved value is the type's procedure, not the scene': A observed the split difference with one retriever and no static arm; Measurement C then measured k3 minus static3 = +17.2 against expert exemplars with no bank-built static arm. This idea manipulates retriever recall (random-type, same-type-random, BM25, oracle same-binding at coverage 0/0.5/1, exact duplicate) and exemplar source on two environments, claims the +17.2 is removed by a fixed bank-exemplar static arm of the goal's type, and claims the recall-to-residual map is flat above type recall on ALFWorld through exact duplicates but rises through product recall on WebShop. Nearest digest card 2604.04949 (trajectory-trained retrievers improve evidence recall and task success): it reports both metrics moving together without a random or fixed control; this idea claims recall gains above the type threshold do not translate to success on template environments and that the translation is set by the bank's duplicate availability. Archived decorative_retriever (5.75) observed overlap; this idea manipulates it at three coverage levels and adds a second environment.
Changes made: P1: restated against Measurement C's +17.2 (the old 'BM25 within ±8 of the best static arm' was already contradicted by C); now names the manipulation that removes the residual (expert exemplars replaced by fixed bank exemplars of the same type: static3-bank within ±8 of BM25) and keeps the step at type recall (same-type-random within ±8 of BM25); added static3-bank and whole-bank so the comparator is built from the same bank; comparator selected on two separate seeds (winner's curse removed); valid_unseen dropped and four fresh seeds on valid_seen restore 560 cells. P2 (was near_entailed): the manipulation moved from the BM25 bank filter with an uncontrolled same-scene rate to the oracle same-scene arm at coverage 0/0.5/1, where per-cell scene recall equals c by construction and a bank supplement guarantees at least one same-scene same-type item per game; added the same-game exact-duplicate rung as the riskiest test; effects are comparator-free paired differences. P3: binding claims moved to the coverable subset S (at least 150 test instructions with a same-product bank success, 4 seeds, at least 600 cells) so the oracle branch cannot fail from a thin same-product rate; the BM25 clause became quantitative (BM25 gain equals b_ws times the oracle gain) with a pre-registered b_ws threshold; comparator fixed out-of-sample on a held-out train set and the whole-bank confound handled by also reporting over the best bank-invariant family; manipulation effects comparator-free so the shared comparator term no longer moves all residuals together. P4 (headline, was near_entailed): now fit on three coverage levels (0, 0.5, 1) plus the natural BM25 point in each environment, linear slope with bootstrap CI and a stated MDE of 16 net per unit coverage; the falsifier is the negation of each clause separately (ALFWorld slope at or above +16; WebShop slope below +8), each producible by named arms. P5: kept as the gate but it now withdraws only the residual-over-static claims; the comparator-free coverage contrasts are tested regardless. Cuts: k=1 length ablations and valid_unseen retrieval cells dropped. Novelty kept: the claim still says ALFWorld retrieval has no residual over the right static prompt and no gain through exact-duplicate recall while WebShop gains through product recall; the +17.2 is explained by exemplar source, a sharper and riskier claim than the old one. Compute: about 10,500 ALFWorld and 20,000-23,000 WebShop episodes, about 27 replica-hours, about 14 h wall-clock on two A100s plus the WebShop setup day.
